prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the camera wearer looking down at a wooden hallway floor in frames 1–2, turning past a narrow doorway wall in frame 3, and stepping through the doorway into an open kitchen and living area in frames 4–5. In frames 1–2, a black backpack on the floor to the lower left and the wearer's extended right hand holding a small spray bottle (frame 1) and blue cloth (frame 2) appear bright at roughly 0.4–0.9 m (within arm's reach), while the floor and base of the wall recede to 1.2–1.8 m. Across frames 4–5, as the wearer approaches and looks up, the wooden door and doorframe on the left and lower-right edges become very bright at 0.2–0.6 m, partially occluding the adjacent room where a standing person on the right holds a vacuum cleaner handle and hose within their arm's reach at roughly 1.5–2.2 m from the wearer, with a vacuum canister on the floor (~1.8–2.2 m), a blue bag (~2.2–2.8 m) behind the canister, and kitchen counters, an oven, and bins further back to the left at 3–4.5 m (about 1.5–2.5 m from the standing person). In frame 5, the wearer's right forearm and hand holding a white vacuum attachment extend forward into the lower right at 0.3–0.5 m, pointing toward the standing person who faces and looks downward toward the wearer and the attachment from roughly 1.2–1.5 m away. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clarifies the 3D step-off between the foreground doorway jambs, the wearer's outstretched hand, and the vacuuming person behind the threshold, though it is unreliable on per-frame scale consistency (frame 3's wall at ~0.5–1.0 m normalizes across the whole range) and loses thin structures like the lower vacuum wand and balcony railings into the dark background.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against an unlabelled black background, picking out the camera wearer's right arm at the bottom of frames 1 and 5 (at ~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach) and the second person standing in the upper right of frame 5 (~1.2–1.5 m away, facing toward the wearer), along with the built-in oven/microwave unit in the upper-left kitchen background (~3.5–4 m away and ~2.5 m to the left of the standing person). In frames 1–2, it outlines the black backpack on the floor to the lower left (~0.8–1.0 m from the wearer and ~0.3 m left of the wearer's hand) and the small bottle held in the wearer's right hand, while in frame 5 it segments the white nozzle attachment held between the wearer's lower-right hand and the standing person's legs. Across the 5 frames, the masks track the wearer turning away from the floor-level backpack in frames 1–2, passing the close wall in frame 3, and extending the attachment toward the standing person who enters the right side of the view in frames 4–5. While the masks clearly separate the boundaries of the wearer's extended arm, the held attachment, and the standing person's torso/shorts from the cluttered floor and railing in frame 5, the semantic labels are heavily unreliable throughout. Specifically, the black backpack is mislabelled as a 'person' in frames 1–2, a wall pillar is labelled 'refrigerator' in frame 1, the white doorframe is labelled 'toothbrush' in frame 3, the held vacuum nozzle is labelled 'person' in frame 5, and the person partially occluded by the doorway in frame 4 as well as the vacuum cleaner and blue bag are completely missed.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders a magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand in frame 1 and yellow body skeletons for the second person standing to the right beyond the doorway in frames 4 and 5. In frame 1, the wearer's right hand is positioned in the lower center-left at roughly 0.5 m (within the wearer's arm's reach, grasping the small bottle above the floor), while frames 2 and 3 contain no detected skeletons as the wearer's hands drop mostly out of view and the wearer turns past the close wall. In frame 4, a partial yellow torso and arm skeleton appears in the upper right at about 2.0–2.5 m where the second person is partly occluded by the right doorframe and faces left toward the vacuum wand in their hands. By frame 5, as the wearer steps closer (~1.2–1.5 m away), the second person's yellow torso, shoulder, and hip joints widen and rotate to face toward the camera wearer, with head keypoints at the top right indicating their head is angled downward toward the wearer's extended right hand. The pose map makes the second person's upper-body orientation and arm articulation through the doorway immediately apparent despite partial occlusion in frame 4 and dark clothing in frame 5, but it is unreliable in missing the wearer's visible hands in frames 2, 4, and 5 as well as the standing person's lower legs and hand keypoints.
